setting: art classroom with easels, clay, brushes, and mountain-window light; navy uniform protected by art smocks when needed

sentences.english: On Monday afternoon, I was drawing a still life in art class.
sentences.japanese: 月曜の午後、美術の時間に静物画を描いていました。

sentences.english: On the desk, there were a red apple, a green leaf, and a brown wooden bowl.
sentences.japanese: 机の上には、赤いりんご、緑の葉っぱ、そして茶色い木のお椀がありました。

sentences.english: With a pencil, I first drew a large circle softly, and slowly changed it into the shape of an apple.
sentences.japanese: えんぴつで、まずやわらかく大きな円を描いて、ゆっくりとりんごの形に整えていきました。

sentences.english: “When you find a shape, first use pale lines softly.
sentences.japanese: 「形を見つけたら、まずは薄い線でやわらかく描いてね。

sentences.english: Later, when you are used to it, use thick lines strongly.
sentences.japanese: 慣れてきたら、濃い線でしっかり描いてみよう。

sentences.english: Then, the picture will become alive,” our teacher said kindly.
sentences.japanese: そうすれば、絵に命が宿ってくるよ」と先生がやさしく教えてくれました。

sentences.english: At the next desk, my sister was drawing a round moon and small stars with straight light.
sentences.japanese: 隣の机では、妹が丸いお月さまと、まっすぐな光を放つ小さな星々を描いていました。

sentences.english: Her paper was full of a quiet night sky.
sentences.japanese: 彼女の画用紙には、静かな夜空がいっぱいに広がっていました。

sentences.english: Tom drew a more abstract picture by putting many shapes together.
sentences.japanese: トムは、いろんな形を組み合わせて、もっと抽象的な絵を描いていました。

sentences.english: “Each shape has its own character,” he said with a serious face.
sentences.japanese: 「一つひとつの形には、それぞれの個性があるんだ」と真剣な顔で言っていました。
